title: Euler increment for the pullback of a tensor product to an integral proper curve
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $C$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] of topological Krull dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $j:C\to X$ be any scheme morphism. Let $\mathcal L,\mathcal M$ be invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-sc-invertible-module]. Suppose $j^*\mathcal M$ is coherent [pqf-def-coherent], where $j^*$ is module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. With sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], coherent Euler characteristic [def-pc-euler-characteristic] and degree [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], one has
$$\chi(C,j^*(\mathcal L\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal M))=\deg_k(j^*\mathcal L)+\chi(C,j^*\mathcal M).$$
No flatness, immersion or dominance hypothesis on $j$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0AYX, lemma-degree-tensor-product, proper-curve case via Tag 0AYV, lemma-degree-on-proper-curve, with generic rank one. Restriction comparison: Modules Tag 01CD, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, and Tag 01CT, lemma-constructions-invertible.

proof.text: Put $A=j^*\mathcal L$ and $B=j^*\mathcal M$. Applying clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] to $j$ and then with the two line bundles interchanged shows that $A$ and $B$ are invertible. In particular both are locally free of rank one [def-sc-invertible-module]. The hypothesis of the item supplies coherence of $B$.

Apply [lem-trf-curve-euler-tensor-generic-rank] on the given integral proper one-dimensional $C$, with its invertible first factor equal to $A$ and its coherent second factor equal to $B$. The generic local ring is $\kappa(\xi)$ as stated there. A local rank-one trivialization of $B$ gives $B_\xi\cong\mathcal O_{C,\xi}=\kappa(\xi)$: take germs of the trivialization and its inverse [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. The image of $1$ is a singleton basis, so its dimension is one [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Thus the cited formula, after $1\cdot\deg_k A=\deg_k A$, gives $\chi(C,A\otimes B)=\deg_k A+\chi(C,B)$.

Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] gives an $\mathcal O_C$-linear isomorphism $e:j^*(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M)\cong A\otimes B$ for this arbitrary $j$. Applying cohomology to $e$ and $e^{-1}$ gives inverse $k$-linear maps in every degree. Hence each cohomology dimension, and therefore the alternating sum defining $\chi$ [def-pc-euler-characteristic], agrees on these two sheaves. Substitute this equality in Step 2 and expand $A,B$ to obtain precisely the asserted formula.

from.place: The fibrewise ampleness-to-projectivity argument: positivity on normalized geometric-fibre components is converted to relative ampleness and then to a projective-bundle embedding. Supporting input: the proper integral curve degree criterion (0B5X). In the 0B5X proof this is the tensor-product degree formula used to pass from the degree of a positive tensor power to the degree of the line bundle and to obtain linear Euler-characteristic growth. Returned proof Step 3: rank-one generic stalk, application of the integral-curve Euler formula, and comparison of the restricted tensor with the tensor of pullbacks.

split_report.summary: Reused the existing generic-rank Euler formula and invertible pullback/tensor theorem; computed rank one explicitly and transported Euler characteristic along the tensor comparison. No new nodes or statement changes.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the returned Step 3 named in blueprint.from.place: rank-one generic stalk, integral-curve Euler formula, and comparison of the restricted tensor with the tensor of pullbacks; this is the existing ampleness/degree support chain under lem-trf-local-term-locality.

tool_uses.why: Generic module-pullback invertibility and tensor comparison, used as a black box; the curve Euler formula does not provide pullback comparisons.

A rank-one trivialization gives B_xi = O_{C,xi} = kappa(xi), so r = 1, which matches Stacks 0AYV (varieties.tex:9669) with n = r = 1. Step 3: clause (2) of the same node gives the pullback-of-tensor isomorphism for any f (Stacks 01CD, modules.tex:2393), and cohomology of an isomorphism preserves chi. proof_deps equals the union of step uses, and there is no cycle. Small cases check out: the identity map with trivial bundles, O(a) and O(b) on P1 including negative degrees, and a constant j. lean.statement: theorem eulerChar_tensorPullback_tensor (k : Type u) [Field k] (C : Scheme.{u}) [C.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsIntegral C] [IsProper (C ↘ Spec (.of k))] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim C = 1) (X : Scheme.{u}) (j : C ⟶ X) (L M : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] [M.IsInvertible] (hM : RingedSpace.IsCoherent C.toRingedSpace ((tensorPullback j).obj M)) : ((tensorPullback j).obj (L ⊗ M)).eulerChar k = ((tensorPullback j).obj L).degree k + ((tensorPullback j).obj M).eulerChar k
